question.text: For higher-volatility asset classes, threshold-based rebalancing typically uses:

answer.text: Wider tolerance thresholds, because they rarely drift
Lower tolerance thresholds and more frequent monitoring, because they have a higher propensity to drift

explanation.text: The Logic: High-volatility asset classes have a higher propensity to drift if left unattended, so the source recommends lower tolerance thresholds and more frequent monitoring for these positions. The Trap: Wider thresholds, no thresholds, or banning the technique altogether all contradict the cited guidance on volatility-aware tolerance bands. Note: The principle "more volatile classes warrant tighter bands" comes directly from the cited source page on threshold rebalancing.
